chunk_findings.detail: In `_cross_family_clean`, a reviewer whose family is equal to `author_fam` is skipped (`_rev_family(r, cfg) != author_fam`), but if `_rev_family(r, cfg)` returns `""` (empty string, representing an unrecognized or unknown family), it is also incorrectly skipped by the condition `_rev_family(r, cfg) != ""`. This means that an unrecognized/unknown reviewer with no findings is treated as a valid "cross-family clean" reviewer, allowing an unknown family reviewer to discount a same-family or known-family reviewer's findings even when no verified independent cross-family reviewer has passed clean. Given an author of family "openai", an unknown reviewer (`family=""`) that returns 0 findings, and a same-family reviewer (`family="openai"`) that returns a finding, `_cross_family_clean` returns `True` because the unknown reviewer is neither empty (skipped by `!= ""`) nor matches `author_fam`, which causes the same-family finding to be incorrectly discounted and the gate to pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:_cross_family_clean

chunk_findings.detail: The stated failure is a prior same-family confirmed finding with no later clean delta (`_confirmed_unrechecked`), while a cross-family reviewer is already clean. `_gate_outcome` still returns `"failed"` whenever `converged_round and _confirmed_unrechecked(it, gate)` and does that before the new `if discounted` pass. Given `converging=True`, a prior review with `chunk_findings`, `_confirmed_unrechecked` true, this round a same-family reviewer still raising findings and a cross-family `REVIEWED` result with no findings, `author_model` resolving to that same family: findings are discounted, `blocking` is empty, then the unrechecked check fails the gate anyway. The discount never runs, so B7dbf432caa stays open on a full re-review.

chunk_findings.detail: When `GD.family_name_of(author_model, cfg.agent.families)` returns `None` and `GD.router_set` returns `None`, the return expression `(bare or GD.family_of(author_model, cfg)).strip().lower() or None` calls `.strip()` on the raw result. If `GD.family_of(author_model, cfg)` returns `None` for an unrecognized name — the exact case the docstring says should produce `None`, and the case the adjacent `_rev_family` explicitly guards with `or ""` — this raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'strip'`. Example: `author_model="unmapped-model"` with no entry in `cfg.agent.families` or `cfg.agent.routers` and `GD.family_of` returning `None` crashes `_blocking_findings` instead of returning `None` and proceeding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:_author_single_family

chunk_findings.detail: The new same-family discount is unreachable in the exact bug B7dbf432caa case. Suppose a same-family reviewer (author family) already has a prior confirmed finding recorded in `gate` and never converges, while gemini/google and grok/xai both return clean. In the full re-review, `_blocking_findings` returns `blocking=[]`, `discounted=[...]`, and `converged_round=True`. Execution then hits `if converged_round and _confirmed_unrechecked(it, gate): return "failed", extra_evidence` before the new `if discounted:` branch, so the prior same-family confirmed finding still blocks and the cross-family clean verdict cannot close the gate. The added comment explicitly says a prior confirmed finding still blocks, which is the opposite of the stated fix requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:_gate_outcome

chunk_findings.detail: When this round is cross-family clean, blocking is `any(fam and fam != author_fam)`. A confirmed unrechecked finding with missing or `""` family (every run recorded before this stamp, and any reviewer whose `family` was never set) makes that predicate false, so `_confirmed_unrechecked` returns False and `_gate_outcome` does not fail. Given a prior gemini/google CONFIRMED digest stored without `family`, gate outcome still `"failed"`, and this round grok/xai `REVIEWED` with no findings, the cross-family defect is discounted and the gate can pass. The same path is what the B7dbf432caa records actually hit: those confirmed findings were written by the old `evidence()["chunk_findings"]` path and have no family, so the discount does not test "same family" at all.

chunk_findings.detail: `LB.full` returning `B.Unavailable` is `continue`d, and if every confirmed digest is only in those blobs, `unresolved` is empty and `_confirmed_unrechecked` returns False even though `it.gate_outcome(gate) == "failed"`. A converged re-review then passes a gate whose recorded findings could not be read, which is the opposite of "must not pass while a confirmed finding stands."
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:_unrechecked_confirmed

chunk_findings.detail: When a previously recorded confirmed finding has no `family` field — e.g. gate evidence stored before `_blocking_findings` started attaching `reviewer`/`family` — `_unrechecked_confirmed` returns `fam=""` for it. In the cross-family-clean branch, `_confirmed_unrechecked` then returns `any(fam and fam != author_fam for _d, fam in unresolved)`. For `fam=""` this expression is false, so the confirmed finding is discounted exactly like a same-family finding. An empty family is not the author family: a pre-existing confirmed finding from a cross-family reviewer (say grok/xai recorded before the family key existed) would be ignored and the gate would pass despite independent cross-family evidence still blocking. The expression should treat `fam=""` as blocking, not discount it.

chunk_findings.detail: `fam_by_digest[digest] = fam` replaces any earlier family, not only a missing stamp. chunk_findings.detail: `setdefault` locks the first non-empty family, but the empty stamp is replaced with `run_fam` before that lock, so a stampless oldest row freezes a fallback family and a later explicit stamp can never correct it. Runs oldest-first: digest D, family missing, `run_fam="deepseek"`, triage confirmed, not cleared by `_cleared_after_delta`; then the same digest with `family="google"`, still confirmed and not cleared. `fam_by_digest[D]` stays `"deepseek"`. The gate discounts an open cross-family confirmation as the author family and can merge. The deleted comment required a later stamp to supersede an earlier stampless row; this rewrite does the opposite.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:fam_by_digest.setdefault

chunk_findings.detail: Using `fam_by_digest.setdefault(digest, fam)` keeps the first non-empty family for a digest, but `fam` has already been forced to `fam or run_fam`, so an earlier row with no explicit family stamp is recorded under the run's identifying family. If that earlier run is the author's own family and a later run stamps the same digest as a cross-family confirmed finding, the returned pair is still `(digest, "<author family>")`, so the gate discounts a still-open cross-family block and can merge it. The previous code explicitly allowed a later explicit stamp to supersede an earlier stampless fallback; `setdefault` regresses that case. Concrete failing input: `runs = [<run family "deepseek", finding D with no family, verdict confirmed>, <run family "google", finding D with family "google", verdict confirmed>]`, with `mine[D]["verdict"] == "confirmed"` and `_cleared_after_delta(...)` false — `fam_by_digest[D]` becomes `"deepseek"` and D is misclassified as author-family.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:278

chunk_findings.detail: `fallback.setdefault(digest, stamp or run_fam)` stores `""` as a real fallback value when the first row has no per-finding stamp and its run family is absent or literal `"unknown"` (`_normalise_family` returns `""` for both). Because `dict.setdefault` does not treat an empty string as missing, a later row for the same digest with no explicit stamp but `run_fam = "google"` cannot replace it. The final `explicit.get(d) or fallback.get(d, "")` then returns `""` for that unconfirmed digest, losing the only non-empty evidence of its family. Concrete input: oldest-first runs with run1 evidence `{"family": "unknown", "chunk_findings": [{"digest": "D"}]}` and run2 evidence `{"family": "google", "chunk_findings": [{"digest": "D"}]}` (both confirmed and not cleared) produce `("D", "")` instead of `("D", "google")`, which can cause the gate to misclassify the open finding.

chunk_findings.detail: `_author_single_family` never normalizes `"unknown"` even though the `_rev_family` sibling explicitly normalizes it because the map/fallback can name `"unknown"`. For an author model whose resolved family is `"unknown"` (for example, an author mapped to the `"unknown"` family or `GD.family_of` returning `"unknown"`), the expression `(bare or GD.family_of(author_model, cfg)).strip().lower() or None` returns the truthy string `"unknown"`, not the documented `None`. chunk_findings.detail: The regression test never constructs the trigger state named in B7dbf432caa. It calls `api.review` exactly once with a fresh first-round same-family `MEDIUM` finding; it performs no delta round and never creates the “confirmed finding with no later delta that re-raised them” row. The bug is specifically about that confirmed-then-unconverged same-family state being treated as merge-blocking. A pre-fix aggregator that already discounts an ordinary first-round same-family finding would return `"passed"` for this exact input, so the test can be green on the unfixed code it is supposed to fail.

chunk_findings.detail: The discount never fires for the state B7dbf432caa describes. Family is taken only from `f.get("family")` on stored `chunk_findings`, and a missing or `"unknown"` stamp is kept as `""`. `_confirmed_unrechecked` then does `any(fam != author_fam for ...)`, so `""` still blocks. A confirmed finding that no later delta re-raised is, by definition, not written again, so a row stored before this stamp (or any evidence path that did not copy `r.family` onto the dict) never acquires a family. Given a prior run whose `chunk_findings` entry for digest D has no `family` key, triage verdict `confirmed`, no later delta clearing D, author family `deepseek`, and this round’s gemini/grok results clean, `_confirmed_unrechecked` returns True and the gate stays `failed`.

chunk_findings.detail: Unreadable evidence fail-closes before the same-family discount, even when the confirmed finding itself was read. `_unrechecked_confirmed` sets `unreadable` if any run’s `chunk_findings` blob is `B.Unavailable`, and the caller returns True immediately. Given run 1’s blob unavailable, run 2 readable with digest D `family=deepseek`, triage confirmed, not cleared after a delta, and a clean cross-family round, the function still returns True and merge stays blocked although D’s family was known.

chunk_findings.detail: The fix only reads the finding family from `f.get("family")` in recorded evidence. The actual B7dbf432caa state is 11 rounds recorded before this change introduced that family stamp, so those same-family `lan-deepseek-v4-pro` confirmed digests have no `family` key and `_unrechecked_confirmed` returns family `""`. `_confirmed_unrechecked` then executes `any(fam != author_fam for _d, fam in unresolved)`; `"" != "deepseek"` is `True`, so it still returns `True` and blocks even when gemini/google and grok/xai are clean. The bug persists for the existing gate; only findings stamped after this change can be discounted.

The new discount path does not get a chance on the very input described by the bug.

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback added for the earlier missing-family case still does not apply to a stored finding whose `family` is `"unknown"` (or whitespace-only): the new line first selects `f.get("family")` before stripping/normalizing, so `"unknown"` becomes `""` and `run_fam` is never used. For the B7dbf432caa state with run evidence identifying the same-family reviewer as `"deepseek"` but the confirmed unrechecked digest stamped `"unknown"`, `fam_by_digest[digest]` remains absent, so `_confirmed_unrechecked` still sees a non-author family and blocks the gate even when a cross-family reviewer passed clean. chunk_findings.detail: The new fallback no longer normalizes `run_fam`: the old expression `(str(f.get("family") or "") or run_fam).strip().lower()` applied `.strip().lower()` to the fallback value, but the new `fam = fam or run_fam` does not. Given `f["family"] == "unknown"` and `run_fam == " DEEPSEEK "` (or `"DEEPSEEK"`), line 273 sets `fam` to that unnormalized string rather than `"deepseek"`. Any downstream comparison against the lowercased same-family marker then fails to recognize the finding as same-family, so the finding is not discounted and the merge can still be blocked.

chunk_findings.detail: `fallback.setdefault` locks in the first value even when that value is empty, so a later stampless row never picks up a real run family. Given run A with `evidence.family` missing and `chunk_findings=[{"digest": "D"}]` (no family), then run B with `evidence.family="deepseek"` and the same stampless digest D, confirmed and not cleared after delta: the first iteration stores `fallback["D"]=""`, the deepseek run does not update it, `explicit` stays empty, and `fam_by_digest["D"]` is `""` instead of `"deepseek"`. The same-family discount therefore cannot see D as author-family, and the merge gate stays blocked on the exact stampless-then-identified shape this aggregator is supposed to resolve. The same first-write also keeps an earlier explicit stamp over a later one (`setdefault` on `explicit`), so a later cross-family stamp on D is discarded.

chunk_findings.detail: In `_cross_family_clean`, a reviewer whose family is equal to `author_fam` is skipped (`_rev_family(r, cfg) != author_fam`), but if `_rev_family(r, cfg)` returns `""` (empty string, representing an unrecognized or unknown family), it is also incorrectly skipped by the condition `_rev_family(r, cfg) != ""`. This means that an unrecognized/unknown reviewer with no findings is treated as a valid "cross-family clean" reviewer, allowing an unknown family reviewer to discount a same-family or known-family reviewer's findings even when no verified independent cross-family reviewer has passed clean. Given an author of family "openai", an unknown reviewer (`family=""`) that returns 0 findings, and a same-family reviewer (`family="openai"`) that returns a finding, `_cross_family_clean` returns `True` because the unknown reviewer is neither empty (skipped by `!= ""`) nor matches `author_fam`, which causes the same-family finding to be incorrectly discounted and the gate to pass.

Given `converging=True`, a prior review with `chunk_findings`, `_confirmed_unrechecked` true, this round a same-family reviewer still raising findings and a cross-family `REVIEWED` result with no findings, `author_model` resolving to that same family: findings are discounted, `blocking` is empty, then the unrechecked check fails the gate anyway. chunk_findings.detail: The new same-family discount is unreachable in the exact bug B7dbf432caa case. Suppose a same-family reviewer (author family) already has a prior confirmed finding recorded in `gate` and never converges, while gemini/google and grok/xai both return clean. In the full re-review, `_blocking_findings` returns `blocking=[]`, `discounted=[...]`, and `converged_round=True`. Execution then hits `if converged_round and _confirmed_unrechecked(it, gate): return "failed", extra_evidence` before the new `if discounted:` branch, so the prior same-family confirmed finding still blocks and the cross-family clean verdict cannot close the gate. The added comment explicitly says a prior confirmed finding still blocks, which is the opposite of the stated fix requirement.

chunk_findings.detail: When this round is cross-family clean, blocking is `any(fam and fam != author_fam)`. A confirmed unrechecked finding with missing or `""` family (every run recorded before this stamp, and any reviewer whose `family` was never set) makes that predicate false, so `_confirmed_unrechecked` returns False and `_gate_outcome` does not fail. Given a prior gemini/google CONFIRMED digest stored without `family`, gate outcome still `"failed"`, and this round grok/xai `REVIEWED` with no findings, the cross-family defect is discounted and the gate can pass. The same path is what the B7dbf432caa records actually hit: those confirmed findings were written by the old `evidence()["chunk_findings"]` path and have no family, so the discount does not test "same family" at all.

chunk_findings.detail: When a previously recorded confirmed finding has no `family` field — e.g. gate evidence stored before `_blocking_findings` started attaching `reviewer`/`family` — `_unrechecked_confirmed` returns `fam=""` for it. chunk_findings.detail: Using `fam_by_digest.setdefault(digest, fam)` keeps the first non-empty family for a digest, but `fam` has already been forced to `fam or run_fam`, so an earlier row with no explicit family stamp is recorded under the run's identifying family. If that earlier run is the author's own family and a later run stamps the same digest as a cross-family confirmed finding, the returned pair is still `(digest, "<author family>")`, so the gate discounts a still-open cross-family block and can merge it. The previous code explicitly allowed a later explicit stamp to supersede an earlier stampless fallback; `setdefault` regresses that case. Concrete failing input: `runs = [<run family "deepseek", finding D with no family, verdict confirmed>, <run family "google", finding D with family "google", verdict confirmed>]`, with `mine[D]["verdict"] == "confirmed"` and `_cleared_after_delta(...)` false — `fam_by_digest[D]` becomes `"deepseek"` and D is misclassified as author-family.

chunk_findings.detail: `fallback.setdefault(digest, stamp or run_fam)` stores `""` as a real fallback value when the first row has no per-finding stamp and its run family is absent or literal `"unknown"` (`_normalise_family` returns `""` for both). Because `dict.setdefault` does not treat an empty string as missing, a later row for the same digest with no explicit stamp but `run_fam = "google"` cannot replace it. The final `explicit.get(d) or fallback.get(d, "")` then returns `""` for that unconfirmed digest, losing the only non-empty evidence of its family. Concrete input: oldest-first runs with run1 evidence `{"family": "unknown", "chunk_findings": [{"digest": "D"}]}` and run2 evidence `{"family": "google", "chunk_findings": [{"digest": "D"}]}` (both confirmed and not cleared) produce `("D", "")` instead of `("D", "google")`, which can cause the gate to misclassify the open finding.

chunk_findings.detail: `origin.setdefault` keeps the first non-empty attribution and no longer lets an explicit per-finding stamp outrank a run-level family. Given runs ordered oldest-first, digest `D` on round 1 with no `family` stamp and `run.evidence["family"] == "deepseek"`, then the same digest on round 2 with `f["family"] == "google"`, the first iteration stores `"deepseek"` and the second is ignored, so the return is `("D", "deepseek")` instead of `"google"`. The deleted path put every non-empty stamp in `explicit` and only used the run family as fallback, so the explicit raiser won regardless of order. A cross-family finding can now be labelled same-family (or the reverse), which is the attribution this gate uses to discount or block merge.

chunk_findings.detail: The new single `origin` map drops the old guarantee that an explicit per-finding family outranks a run-level fallback. `origin.setdefault` keeps the first non-empty attribution, so if the first row for a digest has no per-finding `family` and uses `run_fam` (for example `"deepseek"`), a later row with an explicit per-finding `family` such as `"google"` cannot replace it. The new code returns `D -> "deepseek"`; the old code returned `D -> "google"` because explicit stamps always won. Downstream merge-gate logic can therefore misclassify a cross-family true raiser as same-family (or vice versa), recreating the false-block condition this change is meant to fix.

In the cross-family-clean branch, `_confirmed_unrechecked` then returns `any(fam and fam != author_fam for _d, fam in unresolved)`. For `fam=""` this expression is false, so the confirmed finding is discounted exactly like a same-family finding. An empty family is not the author family: a pre-existing confirmed finding from a cross-family reviewer (say grok/xai recorded before the family key existed) would be ignored and the gate would pass despite independent cross-family evidence still blocking. The expression should treat `fam=""` as blocking, not discount it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:_confirmed_unrechecked

chunk_findings.detail: `fam_by_digest[digest] = fam` replaces any earlier family, not only a missing stamp. With runs ordered oldest-first, a cross-family confirmed finding `digest=D`, `family=google`, triage `confirmed`, not cleared by `_cleared_after_delta`, then a later same-family row of the same digest (`family=deepseek` or run evidence family `deepseek`) makes the returned pair `(D, "deepseek")`. The gate then discounts a still-open cross-family block as the author family and can merge.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:278

chunk_findings.detail: `setdefault` locks the first non-empty family, but the empty stamp is replaced with `run_fam` before that lock, so a stampless oldest row freezes a fallback family and a later explicit stamp can never correct it. Runs oldest-first: digest D, family missing, `run_fam="deepseek"`, triage confirmed, not cleared by `_cleared_after_delta`; then the same digest with `family="google"`, still confirmed and not cleared. `fam_by_digest[D]` stays `"deepseek"`. The gate discounts an open cross-family confirmation as the author family and can merge. The deleted comment required a later stamp to supersede an earlier stampless row; this rewrite does the opposite.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:fam_by_digest.setdefault

chunk_findings.detail: Using `fam_by_digest.setdefault(digest, fam)` keeps the first non-empty family for a digest, but `fam` has already been forced to `fam or run_fam`, so an earlier row with no explicit family stamp is recorded under the run's identifying family. If that earlier run is the author's own family and a later run stamps the same digest as a cross-family confirmed finding, the returned pair is still `(digest, "<author family>")`, so the gate discounts a still-open cross-family block and can merge it. The previous code explicitly allowed a later explicit stamp to supersede an earlier stampless fallback; `setdefault` regresses that case. Concrete failing input: `runs = [<run family "deepseek", finding D with no family, verdict confirmed>, <run family "google", finding D with family "google", verdict confirmed>]`, with `mine[D]["verdict"] == "confirmed"` and `_cleared_after_delta(...)` false — `fam_by_digest[D]` becomes `"deepseek"` and D is misclassified as author-family.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:278

chunk_findings.detail: `fallback.setdefault(digest, stamp or run_fam)` stores `""` as a real fallback value when the first row has no per-finding stamp and its run family is absent or literal `"unknown"` (`_normalise_family` returns `""` for both). Because `dict.setdefault` does not treat an empty string as missing, a later row for the same digest with no explicit stamp but `run_fam = "google"` cannot replace it. The final `explicit.get(d) or fallback.get(d, "")` then returns `""` for that unconfirmed digest, losing the only non-empty evidence of its family. Concrete input: oldest-first runs with run1 evidence `{"family": "unknown", "chunk_findings": [{"digest": "D"}]}` and run2 evidence `{"family": "google", "chunk_findings": [{"digest": "D"}]}` (both confirmed and not cleared) produce `("D", "")` instead of `("D", "google")`, which can cause the gate to misclassify the open finding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:277

chunk_findings.detail: `origin.setdefault` keeps the first non-empty attribution and no longer lets an explicit per-finding stamp outrank a run-level family. Given runs ordered oldest-first, digest `D` on round 1 with no `family` stamp and `run.evidence["family"] == "deepseek"`, then the same digest on round 2 with `f["family"] == "google"`, the first iteration stores `"deepseek"` and the second is ignored, so the return is `("D", "deepseek")` instead of `"google"`. The deleted path put every non-empty stamp in `explicit` and only used the run family as fallback, so the explicit raiser won regardless of order. A cross-family finding can now be labelled same-family (or the reverse), which is the attribution this gate uses to discount or block merge.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:274

chunk_findings.detail: The new single `origin` map drops the old guarantee that an explicit per-finding family outranks a run-level fallback. `origin.setdefault` keeps the first non-empty attribution, so if the first row for a digest has no per-finding `family` and uses `run_fam` (for example `"deepseek"`), a later row with an explicit per-finding `family` such as `"google"` cannot replace it. Concrete input: run1 `evidence.family="deepseek"` with finding `{digest:"D", family:""}`, then run2 `evidence.family="google"` with finding `{digest:"D", family:"google"}`, and `D` is unconfirmed. The new code returns `D -> "deepseek"`; the old code returned `D -> "google"` because explicit stamps always won. Downstream merge-gate logic can therefore misclassify a cross-family true raiser as same-family (or vice versa), recreating the false-block condition this change is meant to fix.
